recent_trades.summary: Initiating a 5% position in GE Aerospace on the successful GEK800 turbofan cruise missile propulsion milestone with Kratos, a concrete program advancement with defense revenue implications.
recent_trades.reasoning: GE Aerospace and Kratos achieved a significant milestone today — successful ignition of the GEK800 turbofan cruise missile propulsion system. This is a concrete program advancement that validates GE's defense propulsion business and signals near-term program revenue. Sentiment is very positive (+0.41). The chart shows GE has been in a tight range ($313-$318) suggesting consolidation before a potential move. This catalyst is distinct from general defense positivity — it's a specific engine ignition test milestone that de-risks the program. With RTX proceeds being freed up, this is an efficient capital rotation within defense. GE sold previously (2026-09-14) but today's program milestone is new, specific information not available at the time of that sale.

Today's headline that Trump may hold off on a major Taiwan arms deal until year-end is a specific, time-bound negative catalyst for RTX's revenue pipeline — Taiwan is a major defense customer. The position is also down -2.22% from entry. With the portfolio nearly fully invested, freeing up ~3% of capital allows redeployment to better-positioned names. The arms deal delay reduces near-term revenue visibility for RTX specifically.
